scenes.heading: The Conductor · live API
scenes.badge: Simulated input: screen events and answers posted as text · synthetic data

captions.text: One server loop decides when Clipa speaks, for web and Mac alike.
It never speaks while you type or talk.
It prepares the question as the screen settles, and asks at the pause.

items.text: A pause: 1.8 s without typing, talking or a screen change
The screen settles 0.5 s after a change; the question is prepared then
Reflect: at most 2 open points, a teach-back of about 60 words
A reworded description of the same screen is not a change

The tutor warns before the mistake. It never blocks another app.

scenes.title: Two people, their agents, one day

items.text: Contracts first: ScreenBridge v1 between two parallel streams
More than 700 automated tests (web 247, agent 190, API 97, screen 179, contracts 24)
CI on every pull request; every merge deploys with a health check and automatic rollback
An engine-agnostic model runner: Claude Agent SDK or Codex CLI
When our Claude quota ran out before the pitch, we switched to Codex without touching the product

scenes.title: What this demo is, and is not

items.text: A teammate plays the expert; all data is synthetic
Off the record stops screen, voice and model calls; it does not recall what was already sent
Confirmed maps live in server memory: one team, one demo server
On Codex, vision takes about 11 s per frame and a question about 13 s after a pause
In these recordings the voice is off: answers and screen events are posted to the live API as text
